ModMetaData.name: Radius UI - Inspector Plus
ModMetaData.author: mrbabilo
ModMetaData.description:
[h1]◆ Radius UI - Inspector Plus ◆[/h1] A fork of [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3786131805]Radius UI - Inspector[/url] by astryl, with [url=https://github.com/keepercraft/RimKeeperFilterHelper]RimKeeper Storage and Filters Helper[/url] by Keepercraft merged into its Storage panel. It replaces both mods: disable them.
[h1]✦ What Plus adds to the Storage panel[/h1] [list] [*][b]Saved filters[/b] shared across saves: apply them in replace, add or remove mode, rename them, overwrite them with the current filter. [*][b]Drag to tick[/b]: drag over checkboxes to set many rows at once. [*][b]Contents list[/b]: what the storage holds, one row per item with its count. Click a row to open it in the filter tree. [*][b]Stock in the tree[/b]: each item row shows how many are stored here, and turns orange when the settings refuse them. A message warns when a change makes stored things leave. [*][b]Special filters that act on the tree[/b]: refusing "fresh", "smeltable" and the like unticks the items it refuses outright; filters that depend on each thing (rotten, tainted) mark the rows they can still turn away. [*][b]Colours[/b]: each top-level category has its colour; special filters are green or red depending on what they let in. [*][b]Item badges[/b]: small icons on each item row show its properties, with a tooltip for each: diet (plant, animal product, meat, insect meat, human meat), toxic (drug, addictive drug, toxic waste, tox gas, poisoning food), fresh produce that needs refrigeration with its days to rot, burnable, smeltable, and apparel restricted to children, men or women. A faded badge means it depends on the material. [*][b]Search that stands out[/b]: the tree's search field has a magnifier and an accent outline, solid while you type. [*][b]Collapse all / Expand all[/b]: one button does both, following the tree on screen. It rests during a search, which already unfolds every match. [*][b]Larger item icons[/b], cropped to the visible art, and a Storage panel height setting. [*][b]Invert[/b]: one button allows every refused item and refuses every allowed one. [*][b]Materials[/b]: refuse steel, wood, a leather or any other material to refuse everything made of it. One row per material the storage can take, with its icon, in a section of its own. Bills, apparel policies and the vanilla storage tab get a "Materials" button above their filter. Replaces Material Filter. [*][b]More special filters[/b]: with or without quality, deteriorating or not, rotting or not, flammable or not, with or without hit points, stackable or not, colony or other animal corpses (from Useful Filters), useless or useful apparel and weapons, with the conditions set in the mod settings (from Useless Filter). Special filters are laid out one row per set of choices (fresh / rotten, smeltable / non-smeltable, every skill book…), each choice a coloured chip, with an "All" chip that allows the whole row. Special filters that do exactly the same thing on a storage are shown once. [*]Replaces [b]Useful Filters[/b], [b]Useless Filter[/b] and [b]Material Filter[/b]: disable them. A save that used them keeps what its storages refused; the useless conditions are copied from Useless Filter's settings file on first start. [b]No Quality Filter[/b] is replaced too: its two filters keep their place in saves. [*][b]Detailed pawn tooltips[/b] (after RimHUD): health by body part, thoughts and their mood effect, bio, trait descriptions, stats behind needs and skills. [*][b]Layout presets[/b]: save the layout of every pawn profile under a name, apply it later in any save, and import RimHUD layouts (its own presets, your RimHUD layout, presets shipped by mods). [*]Works alongside [b][UR] Better Filter[/b] (an "Advanced" button opens its advanced filter; its placeholder items stay out of the tree) and [b]Storage Sorting[/b] (a gear on each row opens its fine-tuning). [/list] Plus is maintained by mrbabilo. Everything below comes from the original Inspector by astryl.
The inspect pane in the bottom left is the panel you look at more than any other, and vanilla gives it a tan box, a wall of grey text, and tabs that drop a window over your colony every time you open one. Radius UI - Inspector replaces it with a dock: a portrait, the things you actually check, and tab buttons that open their content inside the panel. Same flat, dark, icon led look as the rest of the Radius UI suite. Safe to add whenever you want; see below before removing it.
[h1]✦ Tabs open inside the panel[/h1] This is the part to read first. Clicking a tab does not throw a window over your base. The panel grows to fit it in one smooth motion, and the tab draws itself in the space that opened. [list] [*][b]Every tab still belongs to whoever wrote it[/b]: the inspector never redraws another mod's tab, it moves it. Vanilla Health, Bills, Storage, Social and the rest render exactly as they always did, in the panel instead of over it. [*][b]Modded tabs work the same way[/b]: Radius UI - Health Tab shows its full medical chart in there, True RPG Inventory shows its paperdoll. Neither needed a patch, and neither does yours. [*][b]Tabs fill the panel[/b]: a tab narrower than the panel (gear, training, Bio Tab+) spreads over the whole width instead of leaving an empty strip. With Modern Bio Tab, its switch is an icon that no longer covers the card's buttons or Bio Tab+'s header. [*][b]Close it and it shrinks back[/b]: the Overview pill returns the panel to its normal height, so nothing is ever left hanging open. [*][b]It reserves its own space[/b]: the command buttons on the right slide clear as the panel grows, so a wide tab never ends up underneath them. [/list]
[h1]✦ Build the panel you want[/h1] The overview is a grid you arrange, not a fixed list somebody else picked. [list] [*][b]Rows and columns[/b]: put a skill bar across from a need bar, three needs in one row, or a wide health summary on its own. A row holds as many cells as you want. [*][b]Pick from everything[/b]: mood, any single need, any single skill, the whole skills grid, a health summary, the equipped weapon, armor, or a spacer. [*][b]Your own headings[/b]: headers are cells too. Rename them, move them, delete them. [*][b]Edited in place[/b]: press the gear and the editor opens on the panel itself. No menu diving, no restart, and it saves with your game. [/list]
[h1]✦ Not just colonists[/h1] [list] [*][b]Anything you can select[/b]: items, walls, coolers, campfires, plants, corpses and modded buildings all get the same dock. [*][b]Read at a glance[/b]: hit points, fuel and growth as bars, then quality, stack size, value, power draw, and flags like forbidden or broken down as chips. [*][b]Modded things included[/b]: underneath, each thing prints its own report exactly as it always has, so content from any mod reads correctly without a patch. [*][b]Many at once[/b]: select a crowd and you get one row each, portraits and mood for pawns, and a click focuses whichever one you want. [/list]
[h1]✦ Quiet when you are not using it[/h1] [list] [*][b]It folds away[/b]: after a few idle seconds the panel drops to a slim strip and your map is clear. Touch it and it is back. [*][b]Pin it[/b] if you would rather it stayed open, or set your own delay, or turn folding off entirely. [*][b]Wide mode[/b] for larger screens and busier layouts. [/list]
[h1]✦ Built to share the screen[/h1] [list] [*][b]RimHUD[/b]: if RimHUD is running, this mod stands aside completely and notes it once in the log. They will not fight over the pane. [*][b]A way back[/b]: one setting restores the plain vanilla tab row if you ever want it. [*][b]Fails safe[/b]: if drawing ever goes wrong, the pane quietly returns to vanilla instead of flooding your log or spoiling your game. [*][b]Almost nothing in your save[/b]: only the extra special filters and material filters of the Storage panel. Removing the mod mid colony makes the game log warnings about them on load and forget those settings; nothing else is lost. [/list]
[h1]✦ Requirements[/h1] [list] [*][b]Harmony[/b] and [b]Radius UI Framework[/b]. The framework carries the shared colours, icons and widgets for the whole suite. [*][b]RimWorld 1.6[/b]. [/list]
[h3] My Quality Commitment:[/h3] [list] [*] [b]Fully Tested:[/b] Every feature and line of code has been thoroughly tested in-game to ensure it functions as intended and integrates smoothly. [*] [b]Active Support:[/b] I am fully committed to maintaining this mod. If you encounter any bugs, compatibility issues, or unintended behavior, please report them in the comments or a dedicated discussion thread. [*] [b]No Abandonware:[/b] I will actively patch, refine, and update this mod to keep it working and up to standard. [*] [b]No Coffee:[/b] I will never ask for donations for AI created / assisted mods. I share these in the hopes they spark joy for someone, making AI generated content and then begging for money that could go to artists and people more deserving is NOT responsible AI usage. [/list]
